changelog: A FULL RECORDED SCORE AND SOUND SET. Every one of the game's 42 sound cues and all five music beds are now recorded audio rather than synthesized tones, with three alternate takes on the ten cues you hear most often — footsteps, rifle fire, impacts — so a busy turn no longer repeats one sample. THE MUSIC FOLLOWS THE FIGHT. The battle and boss beds each carry a second layer that fades in as your HQ is ground down, or when the boss turns, rather than looping past whatever is happening on the board. Transitions between screens crossfade at constant power, and each bed resumes where it left off, so coming back to the map no longer restarts the track from the top. THE ENEMY TURN SPENDS ITS TIME WHERE IT MATTERS: the replay used to divide its budget evenly, so on a busy turn a unit being destroyed got the same beat as a rifleman shuffling in the distance. A kill now runs half again as long as it did, and distant movement is brief. ENEMY MOVEMENT AND ARRIVALS ARE AUDIBLE — the whole enemy turn used to play out in silence. A unit being destroyed, promoted or healed each have their own sound; a promotion previously reached you through no channel at all, neither seen nor heard.
